PullRequest.Title: agentHost: keep plugin subagents in Copilot catalog
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341680

The Copilot runtime treats any explicitly provided `customAgents` array, including an empty one, as the complete agent catalog instead of merging agents discovered from `pluginDirectories`. Because Agent Host always supplies its built-in agents explicitly, file-plugin siblings disappeared from the `task` tool whenever a plugin parent was selected.

This change projects every enabled plugin agent into `customAgents` while continuing to use `pluginDirectories` for the plugin's other resources. It adds discovery coverage for a multi-agent plugin alongside workspace and user-home agents, plus a real bundled-runtime integration test that selects a plugin parent and successfully delegates through `task` to a sibling from the same plugin.

## Validation

- Passed — `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed — `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotPluginConverters.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --grep 'toSdkSessionCustomAgents|passes a standalone client bundle'` (3 tests)
- Passed — `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotPluginConverters.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` (182 tests)
- Passed — `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts` (17 tests)
- Passed twice — `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/providerIntegration/copilotMockLlm.integrationTest.ts --grep 'selected plugin agent delegates'`
- Passed — `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed — targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed cardinality, sequential `await`, and create/resume critical path are directly traced. Exact delay varies with plugin count and filesystem latency, and discovery may leave the OS cache warm, which is why severity is low rather than suppressing the finding.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem read operations plus frontmatter parsing and prompt-string allocation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Configuration latency now grows serially with the total number of agents across all enabled file-backed plugins; N agents cause N awaited reads with effective concurrency 1 on every non-ephemeral create or resume.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased first-message and session-resume latency, especially when the plugin directory is on a slow or remote filesystem
Findings.PreviousBehavior: File-backed plugin agents were excluded from this host-side conversion and loaded through `pluginDirectories`; only a selected file-backed agent could be added to the serial loop. Thus the host-side pre-session critical path had zero or one reads for those plugins rather than one read per enabled agent.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed `flatMap` feeds agents from every plugin, including file-backed plugins, into `toSdkCustomAgents`; that helper awaits `fileService.readFile` inside a `for` loop, so all newly included plugin files are read sequentially on `_buildSessionConfig`'s critical path.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 182 changed the input from only plugins without file directories (plus at most the selected agent) to `plugins.flatMap(plugin => plugin.agents)`, increasing this serial filesystem boundary from O(non-file agents + selected agent) to O(all enabled plugin agents).
Findings.Title: Avoid serially rereading every installed plugin agent at session launch
Findings.Impact: Creating a normal chat or resuming one now waits for every enabled plugin agent file to be read one after another before `createSession`/`resumeSession` can begin. A plugin catalog with tens of agents on a high-latency filesystem can add the sum of all read latencies to the first prompt or resume.
Findings.Evidence: `toSdkCustomAgents` at lines 115-161 performs `await fileService.readFile(agent.uri)` inside a sequential loop. `_buildSessionConfig` at `copilotSessionLauncher.ts:1185-1188` awaits this promise before constructing the SDK session, and `launch` at lines 900-906 invokes that path for both create and resume. The snapshot is produced after customization discovery, whose `readAgentComponents` already reads agent frontmatter concurrently with `Promise.all`, so there is no retained content cache that makes these launch-time reads free; only the OS cache may be warm.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep projecting all agents, but read/convert them with bounded concurrency while preserving input order (or retain the already-read agent body in the parsed snapshot with proper invalidation) so session startup does not sum one filesystem round trip per agent.

Scenarios.Scenario: First prompt in a newly created non-ephemeral Copilot chat with enabled plugin agents
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first send materializes the provisional chat, waits for customization snapshot/discovery, then `_buildSessionConfig` waits for all custom-agent conversions before the single SDK `createSession` call; only after initialization can the prompt be sent to the model. The changed reads are therefore on the first-prompt critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and parse plugin manifests and agent frontmatter into the applied customization snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per plugin parse/refresh; agent contents are read once per deduplicated discovered agent, concurrently within a plugin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same customization discovery and frontmatter reads already occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot acquisition must settle before launch; this pre-existing discovery work is not introduced by the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read each full agent Markdown file and parse frontmatter/body into `CustomAgentConfig`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential read per deduplicated agent in every enabled plugin; newly includes all agents from file-backed plugins.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File-backed plugin agents were excluded from this host conversion, except at most the selected agent; the SDK received plugin directory paths instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: `_buildSessionConfig` awaits completion before invoking SDK session creation, so latency sums across reads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the SDK session with `customAgents` and `pluginDirectories`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One SDK creation call per materialized chat; its custom-agent payload now contains every enabled agent definition and prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK creation boundary existed, but file-backed plugin agents were represented by directory paths plus at most the selected explicit definition.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing session creation remains on the first-prompt path and cannot begin until the changed reads finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total deduplicated agents across enabled plugins in the applied snapshot. The newly affected subset is agents from file-backed plugins that were previously represented only by `pluginDirectories`, minus at most the one selected agent.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent frontmatter discovery uses `Promise.all` within `readAgentComponents`, but the changed launch-time conversion has effective filesystem concurrency 1 because `toSdkCustomAgents` awaits each read in a `for` loop. One SDK session creation follows.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed snapshot retains agent metadata and URI, not file contents. A recent discovery can leave OS filesystem pages warm, but there is no application content cache or coalescing for launch conversion; each new session rereads every agent. Unreadable files are retried on later launches rather than negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed input cardinality, sequential await, and first-send call path are explicit in repository code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical installed-plugin agent counts and storage latency are not established. Recently parsed files may be warm in the OS cache, reducing wall time, while remote or slow user-home storage and larger plugin catalogs amplify it.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity regression: the PR materially increases serial filesystem fan-out before every normal session creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resuming a persisted non-ephemeral Copilot chat after its SDK session is no longer live
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resume acquires the client and settled customization snapshot, builds session config, rereads all enabled plugin agent files, and only then invokes the single SDK `resumeSession`; the user cannot continue the chat until this chain completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and convert all agent Markdown files while rebuilding resume configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential read per enabled agent for each actual SDK resume.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Host-side resume conversion skipped all file-backed plugin agents other than a selected one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks `_buildSessionConfig`, and therefore blocks `resumeSession` and chat availability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resume the SDK session with rebuilt configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One primary resume call, with an existing possible fallback retry only for custom-agent-not-found errors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The resume boundary and fallback behavior already existed; fewer file-backed definitions were explicitly supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing blocking boundary; the changed filesystem fan-out is placed immediately before it and enlarges the explicit custom-agent payload.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total deduplicated enabled plugin agents for the resumed chat's customization anchors, including multi-root/workspace and installed plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resume operations are sequenced per session lifetime. Within one resume, the newly expanded agent reads are serialized at concurrency 1; the SDK resume boundary occurs once afterward.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No converted-agent cache is shared across sessions or resumes. Metadata discovery may make disk pages warm, but every resume rebuilds strings/configs and retries failed reads.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: create and resume both call the same `_buildSessionConfig`, and the resume paths pass the full plugin snapshot.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Frequency depends on process/session eviction and restart patterns, and latency depends on filesystem warmth. The added O(agent count) serial operations are certain even when duration is small.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported boundary-fanout finding; repeated resumes pay the same expanded serial reread cost.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: `_buildSessionConfig` substitutes `Promise.resolve([])` for custom-agent conversion, so no changed agent-file reads occur before SDK creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an ephemeral SDK session with an empty explicit custom-agent array and existing plugin directories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ephemeral sessions also skipped explicit custom-agent enumeration before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing session-creation boundary; unaffected by the expanded conversion because the branch skips it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Plugin and agent count does not affect this changed branch because explicit enumeration is skipped.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No custom-agent reads are scheduled; one existing SDK create call remains.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No agent content is read or cached by the changed converter for ephemeral sessions. SDK plugin-directory discovery remains as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the `plan.isEphemeral` conditional directly bypasses the changed helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for the changed conversion branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression on this scenario.

Scenarios.Scenario: A selected plugin parent delegates through the `task` tool to a sibling agent
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All sibling definitions are loaded during parent session startup. Once running, the parent model issues one `task` tool call and the subagent performs its existing model/tool work; the diff adds no per-delegation file read or new loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Preload every plugin agent definition into the parent session catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per enabled agent at session startup, not one read per delegation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the selected parent could be force-included; sibling agents from a file plugin were not available through the explicit catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks parent session startup but is off the critical path of later task invocations once the session is live.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Model turns for the parent and delegated subagent through the existing runtime/task mechanism.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The new test exercises one parent turn and one delegated task; production task networking already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The task/model boundary existed, although the sibling was unavailable in this catalog configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for actual delegation, but the production diff changes catalog availability rather than network-call count or scheduling.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Startup scales with total enabled plugin agents, while one delegation selects one sibling by name. Task/model cost scales with delegated calls but that behavior is not added by the production diff.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup agent reads are serialized at concurrency 1. The tested delegation is a single task call; no changed aggregate task concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The sibling prompt is carried in the per-session explicit catalog after startup. There is no additional converter read on each task invocation, but a new or resumed session rebuilds the catalog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for startup loading and high that delegation itself has no newly introduced repeated boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real users may delegate multiple times, but no evidence shows this diff changes per-delegation resource cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate delegation-time performance finding; its only changed cost is the startup fan-out already reported.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and traced normal create, resume, ephemeral, and plugin-sibling delegation paths. One low-severity boundary-fanout regression was reported: all file-backed plugin agent definitions are now reread sequentially on every non-ephemeral session launch. No additional high-confidence regressions were found in test-only changes or delegation execution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
